title: Finding Yourself in a Map With Particles: A Cloud of Guesses, Weighed by What the Lidar Would See From Each, and the Room That Looks the Same From Two Places

questions.question: Why use many guesses instead of one estimate with an error bar?
options: A robot that does not know where it is may be in many places at once, which one estimate cannot say
questions.explanation: The cloud can have several clumps.

questions.question: A thousand particles found the robot to:
questions.explanation: From a cloud over the whole room.

questions.question: Of 10 runs, 50 particles lost the robot how many times?
questions.explanation: The cloud must be thick enough.

questions.question: In a room with nothing in it, the mirror image was taken for the robot in how many of 8 runs?
questions.explanation: It looks the same turned half a turn.

questions.question: Why is there a uniform share in the likelihood of a beam?
options: One wild beam (a person walking by) must not give a good particle a weight of zero
questions.explanation: Robustness to what the map does not contain.

questions.question: Why can the mean of a cloud with two clumps be nowhere?
questions.explanation: Look at the spread and the modes.
